To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carboxyl-terminus of sensor kinases is the primary target for inhibition by compounds that bind to the catalytic domain of sensor kinases and that these compounds cause structural changes in the catalytic domain, leading to aggregation.

the inhibitors of bacterial twocomponent systems target the carboxy-terminal catalytic domain and that the inhibitors cause structural alterations in the sensor kinase leading to aggregation and inhibition of signaling.

inhibitors of the two-component signal transduction system of bacteria bind to the catalytic domain of histidine kinases, causing a conformational change that leads to aggregation of the protein and subsequent loss of function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and development of small molecule inhibitors of bacterial two component systems as a novel approach to the discovery of anti-infective agents.
the identification and characterization of small molecule inhibitors of bacterial signal transduction pathways.
understanding the molecular basis of bacterial virulence and developing novel anti-infective agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism by which these inhibitors exert their effect is to induce structural alterations in the sensor kinase leading to aggregation and loss of activity.
the most potent compounds are targeting the catalytic domain of sensor kinases and are causing aggregation of the protein.
the most potent two-component system inhibitors are those that target the catalytic domain of sensor kinases, causing a conformational change leading to aggregation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhibitors of the two-component systems of pathogenic bacteria can be developed that have the potential to become new anti-microbial drugs.
the most potent two-component inhibitors are those that target the sensor kinase catalytic domain and exert their effects through a noncompetitive mechanism of action.
the most potent compounds identified to date for inhibition of bacterial two-component signal transduction are the 4-quinolones, which target the carboxy-terminal catalytic domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carboxyl terminus of the sensor kinase domain is the target for inhibitors and that these inhibitors work by causing structural changes in the kinase that lead to aggregation.
inhibitors of the two-component system can be designed to target a single protein domain.
compounds that inhibit two-component signaling systems by targeting the kinase domain can cause aggregation.
